label: AuditReport
payload:
React 18 migration audit complete. Key blockers/findings to address before/while migrating:
1) Entry point likely still uses ReactDOM.render/hydrate; must switch to createRoot/hydrateRoot from react-dom/client.
2) Check dependencies for React 18 compatibility: react, react-dom, @types/react, @types/react-dom, testing libraries, router/state libs, and any packages relying on legacy lifecycles or private React internals.
3) Audit class components for deprecated/unsafe lifecycles (componentWillMount/ReceiveProps/Update, UNSAFE_*), string refs, findDOMNode usage, legacy context, and assumptions tied to synchronous rendering.
4) Automatic batching in React 18 may change behavior in async callbacks/timeouts/promises/native events; inspect code that reads state immediately after setState/useState updates and places that may require flushSync.
5) StrictMode in React 18 can double-invoke certain render/effect paths in development; identify non-idempotent effects, duplicate subscriptions, and side effects in render/constructor/effect setup.
6) SSR/hydration paths need review for hydrateRoot, streaming APIs if used, and mismatch-sensitive code.
7) Test setup may need updates: React Testing Library versions, act-related expectations, root API changes, and timing assumptions under concurrent features.
8) Third-party DOM integrations/portals/modals should be reviewed for compatibility with the new root API and StrictMode.
9) If using TypeScript, check updated children/event typings and root container typings.
Recommended phased order: dependencies/root API upgrade first, then class component cleanup, then batching/StrictMode fixes, then full test pass.
